# FSL Sensitivity Analysis
```{r}
library(corrplot)
library(RcppHungarian)
```


### Load 160, 150, 140 versions ###
```{r}
subject_courses_150 <- read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Output/Flica_Output/ABIDE/iterations1500/FSL_format/150ica_secondfilter/subjectCoursesOut.txt')
subject_courses_140 <- read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Output/Flica_Output/ABIDE/iterations1500/FSL_format/140ica_secondfilter/subjectCoursesOut.txt')
subject_courses_160 <- read.table('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Output/Flica_Output/ABIDE/iterations1500/FSL_format/160ica_secondfilter/subjectCoursesOut.txt')

subject_courses_tp_150 <- t(subject_courses_150)
subject_courses_tp_140 <- t(subject_courses_140)
subject_courses_tp_160 <- t(subject_courses_160)

# Remove zero columns
subject_courses_tp_150 <- subject_courses_tp_150[, colSums(subject_courses_tp_150 == 0) != nrow(subject_courses_tp_150)]
subject_courses_tp_140 <- subject_courses_tp_140[, colSums(subject_courses_tp_140 == 0) != nrow(subject_courses_tp_140)]
subject_courses_tp_160 <- subject_courses_tp_160[, colSums(subject_courses_tp_160 == 0) != nrow(subject_courses_tp_160)]

# Correlate subject courses between the two versions
cor_matrix140 <- cor(subject_courses_tp_150, subject_courses_tp_140)
cor_matrix160 <- cor(subject_courses_tp_150, subject_courses_tp_160)
```

# Hungarian plot
```{r}
# if the order is different then the diagonal wont be great -> this is why we use hungarian method. 
# We want max correlation not min cost so we flip it (min cost = high correlation and so on) 

# 140
cost_matrix140 <- 1 - abs(cor_matrix140)
result <- HungarianSolver(cost_matrix140) # This finds the one-to-one pairing (lowest cost / highest correlation)

# result$pairs is a 2-column matrix: [150-IC solution, 140-IC solution]
pairs <- result$pairs                     # Tells us which ICs are best matched
valid <- pairs[, 2] > 0                   # Removes columns with a 0 (because 150 has more ICs than 140)
pairs <- pairs[valid, , drop = FALSE]

match_table <- data.frame(                # A table of each matched pair and its correlation
  ICS_150 = pairs[, 1],
  IC_140 = pairs[, 2],
  correlation = sapply(1:nrow(pairs), function(i) cor_matrix140[pairs[i, 1], pairs[i, 2]])
)

# Correlation plot with strong correlations on the diagonal
cor_matrix_matched <- cor_matrix140[pairs[, 1], pairs[, 2]]


# 160
cost_matrix160 <- 1 - abs(cor_matrix160)
result160 <- HungarianSolver(cost_matrix160)
pairs160 <- result160$pairs
valid160 <- pairs160[, 2] > 0
pairs160 <- pairs160[valid160, , drop = FALSE]

match_table160 <- data.frame(
  IC_150 = pairs160[, 1],
  IC_160 = pairs160[, 2],
  correlation = sapply(1:nrow(pairs160), function(i) cor_matrix160[pairs160[i, 1], pairs160[i, 2]])
)

cor_matrix_matched160 <- cor_matrix160[pairs160[, 1], pairs160[, 2]]
``` 

# Sorted absolute correlation profiles (spaghetti plot)
```{r}
n150 <- ncol(subject_courses_tp_150)
n140 <- ncol(subject_courses_tp_140)
n160 <- ncol(subject_courses_tp_160)

ic_of_interest <- 37  # the significant IC

png('/Volumes/g_psyplafor_methlab$/Students/Katharina_Bremer/Output/Plots/Asorted_correlation_profiles.png',
    width = 16, height = 7, units = "cm", res = 300)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3.5, 3.5, 1.5, 0.5), mgp = c(2.2, 0.6, 0),
    cex = 0.7, tcl = -0.3, las = 1, bty = "l")

# 140
plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, n140), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "Components of 140-IC solution (sorted)",
     ylab = "Absolute correlation")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 140, 20))

for (i in 1:n150) {
  if (i == ic_of_interest) next
  vals <- sort(abs(cor_matrix140[i, ]), decreasing = TRUE)
  lines(vals, col = rgb(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.3), lwd = 0.8)
}
vals <- sort(abs(cor_matrix140[ic_of_interest, ]), decreasing = TRUE)
lines(vals, col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

# 160
plot(NULL, xlim = c(1, n160), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "Components of 160-IC solution (sorted)",
     ylab = "Absolute correlation")
axis(1, at = seq(0, 160, 20))

for (i in 1:n150) {
  if (i == ic_of_interest) next
  vals <- sort(abs(cor_matrix160[i, ]), decreasing = TRUE)
  lines(vals, col = rgb(0.6, 0.6, 0.6, 0.3), lwd = 0.8)
}
vals <- sort(abs(cor_matrix160[ic_of_interest, ]), decreasing = TRUE)
lines(vals, col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

legend("topright", legend = c("IC37", "Other ICs"),
       col = c("black", "grey60"), lty = c(2, 1), lwd = c(2, 1), bty = "n")
dev.off()

#Good robustness = Most lines start high on the left (r ≈ 0.8–1.0) and drop sharply. This means the IC has one strong counterpart in the other decomposition and doesn't correlate much with anything else. 

match_table[match_table$ICS_150 == 37, ]
match_table160[match_table160$IC_150 == 37, ]

summary(abs(match_table$correlation))
summary(abs(match_table160$correlation))
```
